cases.measured: round 6 folds 2026-10-29 (row corrected, was a PASS row): the cv32e40p register file's untyped `localparam NUM_TOT_WORDS = FPU ? (ZFINX ? NUM_WORDS : NUM_WORDS + NUM_FP_WORDS) : NUM_WORDS` (and NUM_WORDS = 2 ** (ADDR_WIDTH - 1)) is built with + and **, which Icarus 12.0 types wider than the 32-bit int of slang and Yosys 0.53 (`N + 1` is 33 bits there, measured with $bits); here its width is only read in dimension and generate bounds, where it is unobservable, and Icarus agreed with the model through round 5 — a recorded over-refusal of the whole-class rule Constant:untyped-width

cases.name: array_oob
cases.measured: Refused since round 6 (2026-10-29), `ArraySel:partial-overhang`: at this parameter point the design holds a constant part select that is only PARTLY outside its vector. IEEE 1800-2023 11.5.1 reads x in exactly the out-of-range bits and changes only the in-range bits of a write, and the model, Icarus 12.0, Yosys 0.53 and slang agreed; Xcelium 24.03-s004 reads the whole select as x and drops the whole write (docs/sv-xcelium-audit.md clusters P1 and P3, 41 shapes, no flag changes it), so the tools split and the model no longer chooses a reading. Until then this row was a simulated match with Icarus. A select wholly outside (x read, no-op write: every tool agrees), a single-bit select and an in-range one are unchanged (rows overhang_read_n3/n5, overhang_write_n1/n6).

Yosys 0.53 eval on the same source agrees with Icarus (w_flat = 00100000, z = ~a[0]). Xcelium 24.03-s004 (the reference simulator; pinned in harness/sv/xcelium_golden.json, row array_oob_inner; xmelab warns BNDWRN on the constant selects) range-checks each packed dimension on its own, like the model: w_flat = 00000000 and z = x, exactly the model's trace, so Icarus and the Yosys front end are the outliers (Verilator, 2-state, masks the index: a third behaviour; docs/sv-xcelium-audit.md, D2). This confirmation is for the BIT-SELECT row only: for a part-select that overhangs an inner dimension Xcelium equals neither the model nor Icarus (docs/sv-xcelium-audit.md, DX1).
oracle_disagreement.retirement_condition: When Icarus checks each packed dimension separately (z reads x and w stays 00000000), this row must fail until its declaration is removed after review.

cases.name: array_oob_part
cases.measured: Refused since round 6 (2026-10-29), `ArraySel:partial-overhang`: at this parameter point the design holds a constant part select that is only PARTLY outside its vector. IEEE 1800-2023 11.5.1 reads x in exactly the out-of-range bits and changes only the in-range bits of a write, and the model, Icarus 12.0, Yosys 0.53 and slang agreed; Xcelium 24.03-s004 reads the whole select as x and drops the whole write (docs/sv-xcelium-audit.md clusters P1 and P3, 41 shapes, no flag changes it), so the tools split and the model no longer chooses a reading. Until then this row was a simulated match with Icarus. A select wholly outside (x read, no-op write: every tool agrees), a single-bit select and an in-range one are unchanged (rows overhang_read_n3/n5, overhang_write_n1/n6). Its declaration `iverilog-packed-inner-part-linearized` (Icarus 12.0 and Yosys 0.53 linearize an out-of-range INNER index, declared 2026-10-27) described a model-versus-Icarus difference on a simulated trace; Xcelium equals neither (docs/sv-xcelium-audit.md DX1), and the row no longer simulates. The declaration was RETIRED from this row (round 6, lane C: a declaration on a row that no longer simulates is checked by nothing); its record is in docs/sv-oracle-disagreements.md, 'Declarations retired in round 6'. The one confirmed part, the element label outside an ascending dimension (asc_oob = q[0][4], Xcelium equals the model, only Icarus and Yosys's front end linearize it), is the declared Icarus row array_oob_asc.

oracle_disagreement.observed: Icarus 12.0 sizes an unbased-unsized fill NESTED under an operator in an input-port actual narrower than the port self-determined and zero-pads the actual to the port width (warning: Padding 2 high bits of the port): a ^ 1-fill at a = 00 reads 0011 where the context reading gives 1111. Verilator 5.042 (the seven two-state outputs over all 32 two-state points) and Yosys 0.53 (prep; flatten; eval, all ten outputs over the same points) agree with the model. Xcelium 24.03-s004 (the reference simulator; pinned in harness/sv/xcelium_golden.json, row hier_fill_ctx; xmelab warns CUVMPW, port sizes differ, and still extends the fill to the port width) equals the model's trace in all 36 cycles, so only Icarus departs (docs/sv-xcelium-audit.md, D3).
oracle_disagreement.retirement_condition: When Icarus evaluates the nested fills at the port width, this row must fail until its declaration is removed after review.

oracle_disagreement.observed: Icarus 12.0 (macOS, Homebrew) represents the variable y, whose bits 3:2 are a leaf of the concatenated continuous target {y[3:2], z} and whose bits 1:0 have no driver, as a net and reads the undriven bits as z (y = 10zz for x = 101); the model keeps the variable's initial x (y = 10xx). The same lowering as the other partial-variable rows, reached through a concatenation target. Yosys 0.53 prep; eval reports y[1:0] as used but undriven (Missing value for y[1:0]); its synthesized netlist simulated in Icarus reads them as x. Xcelium 24.03-s004 (the reference simulator; pinned in harness/sv/xcelium_golden.json, row concat_undriven) keeps the variable's initial x in the untouched bits and equals the model's trace exactly in every cycle, so only Icarus departs (docs/sv-xcelium-audit.md, D1). In Xcelium a variable reads x and a net reads z; Icarus re-declares a variable with a continuously driven bit as a net.

oracle_disagreement.reference: IEEE 1800-2023 11.5.1 (x[b -: w] selects the w bits from label b DOWN to label b-w+1; a part partly out of range reads x in exactly its out-of-range bits) and 7.4.1 (a single-element range [7:7] has one bit, label 7); slang 11 constant evaluation of the same select over localparam logic [7:7] U = 1 gives U[8 -: 2] = 2'bx1; docs/sv-oracle-disagreements.md#single-element-range-direction
oracle_disagreement.observed: At L = 7 the input u is logic [7:7] and w = u[L+1 -: 2] = u[8 -: 2]. Icarus 12.0 (macOS, Homebrew) evaluates a -: part-select over a single-element range as the +: part-select with the same base (labels b+w-1 down to b, here 9:8, all out of range), so w reads xx in every cycle; the LRM selects labels 8:7, w = {x, u[7]}, which the model gives (x1, x0, xx, xz). Yosys 0.53 chparam -set L 7; prep; eval agrees with the model (w = x1 at u = 1, x0 at u = 0). Xcelium 24.03-s004 (the reference simulator; pinned in harness/sv/xcelium_golden.json, row array_param_labels_l7; xmelab warns BNDWRN) reads w = xx in every cycle, the same as Icarus, but only because Xcelium returns all x for ANY part-select that is partly out of range (docs/sv-xcelium-audit.md, P1: a departure from 11.5.1 that the model does not follow): its value trace neither confirms nor contradicts the Icarus lowering described here. Its elaboration diagnostic does corroborate the label set: for the same select as a continuous-assign target xmelab prints BNDIPERR with the LRM range (u[8 -: 2] over [7:7] is [8:7], never Icarus's 9:8; 38 of 38 -: cases over [7:7] and 38 of 38 over [0:0], verifier run of the audit, docs/sv-xcelium-audit.md, DX2).
oracle_disagreement.retirement_condition: When Icarus reads u[8 -: 2] over [7:7] as labels 8:7 (w = {x, u[7]}), this row must fail until its declaration is removed after review.

cases.measured: Refused since round 6 (2026-10-29), `ArraySel:partial-overhang`: at this parameter point the design holds a constant part select that is only PARTLY outside its vector. IEEE 1800-2023 11.5.1 reads x in exactly the out-of-range bits and changes only the in-range bits of a write, and the model, Icarus 12.0, Yosys 0.53 and slang agreed; Xcelium 24.03-s004 reads the whole select as x and drops the whole write (docs/sv-xcelium-audit.md clusters P1 and P3, 41 shapes, no flag changes it), so the tools split and the model no longer chooses a reading. Until then this row was a simulated match with Icarus. A select wholly outside (x read, no-op write: every tool agrees), a single-bit select and an in-range one are unchanged (rows overhang_read_n3/n5, overhang_write_n1/n6). Its declaration `iverilog-single-element-minus-select` (Icarus 12.0 reads u[L+1 -: 2] over [7:7] as the +: select, declared 2026-10-28) is kept as the record of that Icarus lowering, but the row no longer simulates: the select [8:7] over [7:7] is partly out of range, which is refused here (docs/sv-xcelium-audit.md DX2).

oracle_disagreement.reference: IEEE 1800-2023 9.2.2.2.1 (the implicit sensitivity list of always_comb includes the expansions of the longest static prefix of every read, except an expression also written within the block: the second block reads t, expansion t[1] and t[0], and writes only t[1], so t[0] belongs in its list); 6.5 ("Each bit in a packed type is also an independent element") and 9.2.2.2 ("multiple assignments made to independent elements of a variable are allowed as long as their longest static prefixes do not overlap") make the design LEGAL, as ls-sv's bit-granular one-driver rule admits it; docs/sv-oracle-disagreements.md
oracle_disagreement.observed: Icarus 12.0 (Homebrew, macOS), without a diagnostic, leaves ALL of t out of the second block's sensitivity list (`iverilog -g2012` netlist: its event is `.event anyedge, b` alone) because the block writes t[1], so a change of t[0] (written by the first always_comb; also with `assign t[0] = a;`) does not wake it and y keeps the previous t[0] until b changes (stale at cycles 1, 3 and 5). Xcelium 24.03 (fleet gate refsim on vip-ng, one batched testbench with the other two rows, WP4 round 3) gives exactly the model's trace on all 7 cycles, x included; Verilator 5.042 (--binary --timing, two-state) gives it with x read as 0. The same departure reaches further admitted designs, measured by the round-3 WP4 verifier with Xcelium 24.03 = model: a dynamic read `y = t[s]` (x_dyn) and a child output port driving t[0] (x_child); docs/sv-oracle-disagreements.md lists the class. Which reads Icarus drops (round 6 lane B, from the D4 triage and its verifier: Icarus 12.0 against Xcelium 24.03-s004, Verilator 5.042 and Yosys 0.53, minimal repros, a 48-step stimulus): the Icarus gap is WHOLE-VECTOR reads only -- `y = t` and the constant part-select `y = t[1:0]` are stale (25 of 48 steps each; 15 of 48 with the writer on bit 1 and 11 of 48 with `assign t[0] = a`), while the read of the unwritten bit `y = t[0]` and the concatenation `y = {t[1], t[0]}` are NOT (Icarus prints `sorry: constant selects in always_* processes are not currently supported (all bits will be included)` and includes every bit); `always @*` in place of the second `always_comb` is fine in Icarus; Xcelium, Verilator and Yosys give y = {b, a} on every shape. Only Icarus departs, so the row stays a declared Icarus departure and the model is not changed (the model equals Xcelium's pinned trace on all 7 cycles).

oracle_disagreement.reference: IEEE 1800-2023 11.5.1 (Vector bit-select and part-select addressing, printed page 296): 'Part-selects that are partially out of range shall, when read, return x for the bits that are out of range', with the base expressions evaluated in a self-determined context; slang, Icarus 12.0 and Yosys 0.53 follow it; docs/sv-oracle-disagreements.md, 'Run-time part-select bases that leave the vector'; docs/sv-xcelium-audit.md, cluster P2 and 6.1
oracle_disagreement.observed: Xcelium 24.03-s004 (the reference simulator, default flags; pinned in harness/sv/xcelium_golden.json, row partsel_dyn) treats an indexed part-select READ whose RUN-TIME base leaves the vector for some of its bits and not for others as wholly invalid and returns all x for the whole select, where the model, Icarus 12.0 and Yosys 0.53 return the in-range bits and x only for the out-of-range ones. dyn_up = v[sel +: 4] at sel = 5, 6, 7 and dyn_dn = v[sel -: 4] at sel = 0, 1, 2 (v = 10000001, sel = 101: dyn_up is x100 in the model, xxxx in Xcelium). 6 of the 22 part-select cells of this row are partly out of range: Xcelium is all x on those 6 and equals the LRM value on the other 16 (in range, wholly out of range, x/z base), and the model equals an independent LRM oracle on all 22; Icarus equals the model in every cycle. Xcelium prints no warning by default (IIFAOB / IIRAOB only under -ii_warn -ii_rwarn); the result is not a time-zero race and does not depend on the stimulus order or on the context (verifier probes: 864 cells in assign, always, function and testbench contexts). The same Xcelium rule drops the whole write and reads all x for CONSTANT bases, where it is REFUSED (ArraySel:partial-overhang); a run-time base cannot be refused statically, so the departure is declared, not followed. svGolf's fourstate stage refuses run-time selects that can leave their declared range (svgolf/README.md). -ii_val does not repair module-level reads (docs/sv-xcelium-reference.md, section 6).
oracle_disagreement.retirement_condition: When Xcelium reads a run-time-base part-select that is partly out of range per bit like the LRM (in-range bits kept, x for the out-of-range ones: another Xcelium version, or a flag that applies at module level), the pinned trace equals the model's and the harness fails ('disagreement resolved'; diff_test2.py --golden, or a live xrun run) until the declaration is removed after review; it is also removed, and the row becomes a refusal row, when ls-sv refuses a part-select whose run-time base can leave the vector.
